value: scampi in turbulent flow reached the mussel (Perna canaliculus) bait 44% faster and with lower mean heading angles than in laminar flow
units: categorical (time to reach bait; heading angle)
method: flume odour-plume tracking: each scampi released downstream of a 5 g bait in a laminar or turbulent flow regime; 30 min per trial; bait type mussel gonad or jack mackerel tissue
conditions: 100 scampi obtained from 300 m on the Chatham Rise, 250 km off eastern New Zealand, in July 2015 by short-duration bottom trawl and held in individual enclosures in tanks under red light; flume 1.5 x 0.5 x 0.3 m with 10 um and carbon filtered seawater at 10.5 C; 5 g of defrosted bait in a PVC mesh bag at antennule height (a bait mass, not an odour concentration); 60 experiments, 15 per bait-by-flow combination; 28 females and 32 males; flow regime affected heading angle (t 1,38 = 2.78, P = 0.008, both baits; mussel 15.2 degrees lower in turbulent flow, t 1,17 = 2.07, P = 0.048) and tortuosity (t 1,38 = 3.04, P = 0.004); reached the bait: turbulent 12 of 15 mussel and 14 of 15 mackerel, laminar 9 of 15 mussel and 12 of 15 mackerel

source.title: Orientation and food search behaviour of a deep sea lobster in turbulent versus laminar odour plumes

quote: Scampi in the turbulent flow reached the mussel bait 44% faster and with lower mean heading angles than in laminar flow.
note: Classification: behavioural response of a wild-caught animal to a bait odour plume; no chemoreceptor is identified and flow regime, not odour concentration, was the manipulated variable. Mackerel bait is mixed, not null: the abstract says 'there was no difference between the flow regimes for the mackerel bait' and the mackerel heading-angle reduction was not significant (t 1,19 = 1.83, P > 0.05), but search paths were '24.8% more direct to the mackerel bait (t 1,19 = 2.18, P = 0.038)' and 52.2% more direct to the mussel bait (t 1,17 = 2.10, P = 0.045) in turbulent flow, and 'the increasing walking speed was more pronounced in scampi responding to mackerel bait in a turbulent flow versus those in a laminar flow (F 1,44 = 13.15, P = 0.001)'. Nulls from the same paper: flow regime did not alter success rates overall (G 1 = 5.03, P > 0.05), for mackerel (G 1 = 1.20, P > 0.05) or mussel (G 1 = 1.45, P > 0.05); the Discussion says 'The current study did not observe a difference in mean walking speed due to the two flow regimes' (no statistic printed); sex and size did not significantly affect the orientation parameters, search period or total time to bait.
